newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: The following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:
In response to a question, spokesman Thierry Daman said that at first sight the EU had no specific interest in the financial commitment made on Wednesday by Microsoft Computers to Apple Computers.

Daman said also that the European Commission was acting within its rights to insist on certain standards to be maintained on imports of tallow and other animal by-products from non-EU countries to the 15-nation bloc even if the exporting country had no record of BSE risk. He was responding to a questioner who asked if it was fair for the EU to impose new production standards at short notice on non-EU exporters, particularly the U.S. He said the "modalities" of the new regulations were still being examined.

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said reports in certain media that the Commission, the German government and car manufacturer VW were close to settling differences over a row on state aid to some plants in former East Germany were "premature". In response to a question, she said the fundamental principle remained that such state aid was illegal, and until it had been repaid a solution was unlikely.

Spokesman Constantin Verros, asked for comment on recent strengthened links between Turkey and northern Cyprus, said the Commission was steadfast in urging both the north and south of the divided Mediterranean island -- in conjunction with Greece and Turkey and under the auspices of the United Nations -- to continue to work for a permanent political solution.
The Commission released the following documents:

- IP/97/744: EU wins guarantees from U.S. to change rules regarding "country of origin" requirements on European exports of so-called flat fabrics imported to the EU for dyeing, cutting and printing and then exported as "Made in Europe" products. The U.S. had threatened to block such imports unless they detailed where the original fabric came from.
- IP/97/745: European Commission authorises acquisition by Norsk Alcoa and Elkem of joint control over Elkem Aluminium in the primary aluminium market.
- Memo/97/73: Situation and outlook report on EU cereals, oilseeds and protein crop production.
